person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: We develop an algorithm that can detect pneumonia from chest X-rays at a level exceeding practicing radiologists.

span.label: pneumonia detection on chest radiographs
span.quote: However, detecting pneumonia in chest X-rays is a challenging task that relies on the availability of expert radiologists.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: CheXNet is a 121-layer Dense Convolutional Network (DenseNet) (Huang et al., 2016) trained on the ChestX-ray 14 dataset.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the binary cross entropy is weighted by the prevalence of the OPPOSITE class - w+ is the negative share and w- the positive share - so the rarer label carries the larger weight
span.quote: For a single example in the training set, we optimize the weighted binary cross entropy loss L(X, y) = −w+ · y log p(Y = 1|X) −w− · (1 − y) log p(Y = 0|X), where p(Y = i|X) is the probability that the network assigns to the label i, w+ = |N |/(|P |+|N |), and w− = |P |/(|P |+|N |) with |P | and |N | the number of positive cases and negative cases of pneumonia in the training set respectively.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: dense connections improve the flow of information and gradients through the network, which is what the paper credits for making the optimization of a very deep network tractable
span.quote: DenseNets improve flow of information and gradients through the network, making the optimization of very deep networks tractable.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the network is not trained from scratch: the final layer is replaced and the rest starts from ImageNet weights
span.quote: We replace the final fully connected layer with one that has a single output, after which we apply a sigmoid nonlinearity. The weights of the network are initialized with weights from a model pretrained on ImageNet

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the learning rate is cut only when the validation loss stops improving, and the returned model is the best validation checkpoint rather than the last
span.quote: We use an initial learning rate of 0.001 that is decayed by a factor of 10 each time the validation loss plateaus after an epoch, and pick the model with the lowest validation loss.

span.label: that this makes reader agreement the standard rather than the presence of disease is already recorded on this record as a limitation, not claimed here
span.term: each radiologist and the model are scored against the OTHER FOUR radiologists' labels, taken as ground truth, and the reported figure is the mean of those four scores
span.quote: We compute the F1 score for each individual radiologist and for CheXNet against each of the other 4 labels as ground truth. We report the mean of the 4 resulting F1 scores for each radiologist and for CheXNet, along with the average F1 across the radiologists.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: significance is taken from the DIFFERENCE between the two averages computed on the same bootstrap samples, and read off whether the 95% CI on that difference contains zero
span.quote: To determine whether CheXNet’s performance is statistically significantly higher than radiologist performance, we also calculate the difference between the average F1 score of CheXNet and the average F1 score of the radiologists on the same bootstrap samples. If the 95% CI on the difference does not include zero, we conclude there was a significant difference between the F1 score of CheXNet and the F1 score of the radiologists. We find that the difference in F1 scores — 0.051 (95% CI 0.005, 0.084) — does not contain 0, and therefore conclude that the performance of CheXNet is statistically significantly higher than radiologist performance.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the heatmap is the weighted sum of the final convolutional feature maps, weighted by the final classification layer's own weights for that pathology, then upscaled and overlaid
span.note: about this quote: Q-616, 2026-08-16: FAILED GLYPH INSIDE THIS QUOTE. The staged text reads "Formally, Mc = (cid:88) k wc,kfk" - (cid:88) is the SUMMATION SIGN, so the formula is Mc = sum over k of w_c,k * f_k, the weighted sum of feature maps the sentence has just described in words. The prose on either side is intact and states the mechanism; only the symbol is lost. The quote is an exact substring of the staged file; the file is incomplete here, not the tag. Detected by TOOLS/test_damaged_quote_is_annotated.py.
span.quote: To generate the CAMs, we feed an image into the fully trained network and extract the feature maps that are output by the final convolutional layer. Let fk be the kth feature map and let wc,k be the weight in the final classification layer for feature map k leading to pathology c. We obtain a map Mc of the most salient features used in classifying the image as having pathology c by taking the weighted sum of the feature maps using their associated weights. Formally, Mc = (cid:88) k wc,kfk. We identify the most important features used by the model in its prediction of the pathology c by upscaling the map Mc to the dimensions of the image and overlaying the image.

span.label: the paper identifies three limitations of its radiologist comparison
span.note: what this limits: the radiologist comparison, which the authors themselves qualify: WE IDENTIFY THREE LIMITATIONS OF THIS COMPARISON
span.quote: We identify three limitations of this comparison.

span.label: The paper announces three limitations of the radiologist comparison but enumerates only two (a 'First' and a 'Third'); the second is missing from the text.
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[0] · what this limits: the completeness of that qualification: the paper announces three limitations and prints a FIRST and a THIRD with no SECOND. Verified in the version of record, arXiv 1711.05225v3 (25 Dec 2017), not only in our staged copy - so this is the paper's own text and not a lost sentence in extraction
span.quote: We identify three limitations of this comparison.

span.label: Only frontal radiographs were shown to both model and radiologists, although a share of accurate diagnoses requires the lateral view.
span.note: what this limits: the diagnostic setup for both model and radiologists: ONLY FRONTAL RADIOGRAPHS WERE PRESENTED ... BUT IT HAS BEEN SHOWN THAT UP TO 15% OF ACCURATE DIAGNOSES REQUIRE THE LATERAL VIEW
span.quote: First, only frontal radiographs were presented to the radiologists and model during diagnosis, but it has been shown that up to 15% of accurate diagnoses require the lateral view (Raoof et al., 2012); we thus expect that this setup provides a conservative estimate of performance.

span.label: Neither model nor radiologists could use patient history, which is known to change radiologist diagnostic performance.
span.note: what this limits: the comparison against clinical practice: NEITHER THE MODEL NOR THE RADIOLOGISTS WERE ... PERMITTED TO USE PATIENT HISTORY, WHICH HAS BEEN SHOWN TO DECREASE RADIOLOGIST DIAGNOSTIC PERFORMANCE
span.quote: Third, neither the model nor the radiologists were not permitted to use patient history, which has been shown to decrease radiologist diagnostic performance in interpreting chest radiographs (Berbaum et al., 1985; Potchen et al., 1979);

span.label: The standard the model is measured against is the other radiologists' labels, not the presence of disease.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that this model exceeds practicing radiologists: the F1 score for each radiologist and for the model is computed against each of the other four radiologists' labels as ground truth, so the comparison is agreement with those four rather than detection of disease
span.quote: We compute the F1 score for each individual radiologist and for CheXNet against each of the other 4 labels as ground truth

span.label: The training labels were produced by text extraction from reports rather than by anyone looking at the images.
span.note: what this limits: the labels this model was trained on: they were assigned by automatic extraction methods applied to radiology reports, so a label records what a report said rather than what an image shows
span.quote: annotate each image with up to 14 different thoracic pathology labels using automatic extraction methods on radiology reports

span.label: Every image the extractor did not mark becomes a negative example.
span.note: what this limits: the negative class in this task: images are negative when pneumonia is not among the annotated pathologies, so absence of a label is used in place of absence of the condition
span.quote: We label images that have pneumonia as one of the annotated pathologies as positive examples and label all other images as negative examples

span.label: The model reports fourteen findings while the headline number describes one of them.
span.note: what this limits: the performance figure quoted for this model: the network outputs a vector of binary labels over fourteen pathology classes, while the radiologist comparison concerns the pneumonia task alone
span.quote: instead of outputting one binary label, ChexNet outputs a vector t of binary labels indicating the absence or presence of each of the following 14 pathology classes

span.label: a deep convolutional network (DenseNet) applied to detect disease from chest X-rays at radiologist level
span.quote: a 121-layer convolutional neural network trained on ChestX-ray14

span.label: four practising academic radiologists annotating the same test set, used as the comparison for the model
span.note: eliminates: a number that looks good against no reference - the baseline here is people doing the task on the same images
span.quote: Four practicing academic radiologists annotate a test set, on which we compare the performance of CheXNet to that of radiologists.

span.quote: We compute the F1 score for each individual radiologist and for CheXNet against each of the other 4 labels as ground truth

span.label: a pathology label - AS A FACT ABOUT A REPORT, NOT AN IMAGE: the fourteen labels are assigned by automatic extraction from radiology reports, so the target the network learns is what a radiologist wrote down, filtered through a text-mining tool
